name: Gold bar
description: A heavy cast bar of gold, a litre of it, stamped on top. Worth little now except as metal.
notes: Cast as stacked 4 mm layers tapering 10 mm a side, 175 by 80 mm at the base and 84 mm tall, with a raised stamp plate on top. The five one-litre bars share this shape and differ in finish and mass. The bounding box counts the air round the taper. metal-gold draws it.

name: Lead bar
description: A dull grey cast bar of lead, soft enough to dent with a thumbnail.
notes: Cast as stacked 4 mm layers tapering 10 mm a side, 175 by 80 mm at the base and 84 mm tall, with a raised stamp plate on top. The five one-litre bars share this shape and differ in finish and mass. The bounding box counts the air round the taper. lead draws it.

name: Platinum bar
description: A pale cast bar of platinum, heavier than it looks.
notes: Cast as stacked 4 mm layers tapering 10 mm a side, 175 by 80 mm at the base and 84 mm tall, with a raised stamp plate on top. The five one-litre bars share this shape and differ in finish and mass. The bounding box counts the air round the taper. metal-platinum draws it.

name: Silver bar
description: A bright cast bar of silver, a litre of it, stamped on top.
notes: Cast as stacked 4 mm layers tapering 10 mm a side, 175 by 80 mm at the base and 84 mm tall, with a raised stamp plate on top. The five one-litre bars share this shape and differ in finish and mass. The bounding box counts the air round the taper. metal-silver draws it.

name: Tin bar
description: A silvery cast bar of tin, light for its size.
notes: Cast as stacked 4 mm layers tapering 10 mm a side, 175 by 80 mm at the base and 84 mm tall, with a raised stamp plate on top. The five one-litre bars share this shape and differ in finish and mass. The bounding box counts the air round the taper. No tin or pewter finish exists, so steel-stainless stands in; it reads close to the silver and platinum bars.

name: Cast iron chunk
description: A broken piece of cast iron with rough edges. Heavy enough to throw, or to melt down.
notes: Three irregular slabs stacked into a lump about 52 by 34 by 28 mm. The bounding box counts the air round the irregular outline. iron-cast draws it.

name: Cast iron lump
description: A heavy, misshapen lump of cast iron broken from something larger.
notes: Three irregular slabs stacked into a lump about 76 by 50 by 44 mm. iron-cast draws it.

name: Aluminium bar
description: A small cast bar of aluminium, light and dull grey. Soft metal, but it will knock in a nail.
notes: The gold bar's tapered casting scaled down to 80 by 35 by 34 mm, in alu-bare.

name: Copper tube
description: A length of thin copper water tube. Too light to fight with, but handy for stills and plumbing.
notes: A hollow tube 600 mm long and 22 mm across with a 1.2 mm wall, held by its middle. The explosively pumped flux compression generator is a different object and is left off this model; it needs its own model in a later batch. The size is a placeholder for a thing longer than a pack is deep.

name: Steel pipe
description: A length of threaded steel pipe. A good club, and the start of a lot of makeshift work.
notes: A hollow half-inch pipe 600 mm long and 21 mm across with a 2.6 mm wall and a bright threaded band at each end, held by its middle. The makeshift crowbar variant shares this model as a plain pipe; a flattened, bent end would need its own model, and it should also bring prying. The size is a placeholder.

name: Metal fan blades
description: A five-bladed steel fan taken off its motor, the kind from a big desk fan or an oven.
notes: Five flat paddle blades 300 mm across round a domed hub with a dark shaft bore, lying face up. The blades are drawn flat: pitching them needs a twisted prism the compound family lacks. steel-galvanised draws the blades and steel-grey the hub.

name: Heavy wire rack
description: A sturdy steel rack from an oven or a grill, good for cooking over a fire.
notes: A 600 by 400 mm frame of 6 mm rod round eleven 4 mm cross wires on two runners, in steel-stainless. The box is only 10 mm deep. Cooking over a fire with it has no quality name in use yet.

name: Hinge
description: A heavy steel butt hinge with screw holes in both leaves, for a door or a chest lid.
notes: A 100 mm hinge opened flat: two 3 mm leaves either side of a 10 mm knuckle with its pin ends showing, three screw holes painted dark in each leaf. The hinge itself is about 30 ml.

name: Length of rail
description: A one-metre length of railway rail, smooth on top and rusty everywhere else. Far too heavy to carry far; sawn in half it makes an anvil.
notes: A flat-bottomed rail 172 mm tall on a 150 mm foot, built from four convex pieces, with a worn bright running top and two fishplate bolt holes at one end. The box counts the air round the I-shaped section. scrap-rusted draws the rail and steel-bright the running top. The size is a placeholder for a thing too long and heavy for a pack.

name: Half length of rail
description: Half a metre of railway rail with a flat, smooth top. Set on a stump, it serves as a rough anvil.
notes: The same rail section as the full length, 500 mm long. The box counts the air round the I-shaped section. The size is a placeholder.
